 REMINDER: Clocks “fall back” an hour as daylight saving time ends Sunday morning 
 by 
 Nick Perkins 
 5 minutes ago October 31, 2026

 CASPER, Wyo. — This is one of those good news/bad news situations. The good news is, clocks “fall back” an hour on Sunday, allowing for one extra hour of sleep. The bad news is that it gets darker earlier.
 Daylight savings times is used in most states, beginning in the spring, to take advantage of sunlight being later in the daytime. When days get shorter, in the fall, crop harvesting has concluded and the extra sunlight is no longer necessary. 
 On Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., clocks will reset to 1 a.m., which will give people an extra hour of sleep, but less evening sunlight. When they wake up, people may need to wind back their analog clocks.
